Used both for thanks (wazawaza arigatou) and to wave off effort (wazawaza konakute ii yo).

Escalating amount or pace (dondon samuku naru) and the host's 'dig in' (dondon tabete). Borders on C (manner).

freqNote: 何となく #2554 and kana なんとなく #4044 are counted separately

Grounds a claim in reality (jissai yatte miru to muzukashii).

freqNote: 本気で unsplit #2918; rank of 本気 includes bare 'honki?'

Reverses the expected comparison (mushiro kocchi no hou ga ii).

freqNote: たまたま #1139; noun 偶然 #1011

freqNote: 適当に is not a token; rank of 適当

Close in place, in time (chikai uchi ni) and in relationships; constant in directions and plans.

Clean, register-neutral topic change.
'Or' between two questions ('koohii? soretomo ocha?').
Embeds a yes/no question in any sentence ('iku ka dou ka wakaranai').

freqNote: そしたら #557; full そうしたら #6072

Concession across sentences: despite all that.

Adds a further reason or point to an argument.

freqNote: ってことは #1037; ということは #1439

Redirects the conversation to what matters more.

freqNote: なので #652, includes clause-final na node

freqNote: tokenizer splits じゃないと; rank of polite でないと

Accusatory 'even though you...'; common in what you hear, use sparingly.

freqNote: no usable rank — judgement (tokenizer splits; たら #2818)

A wishful ending (hayaku konai kana).

freqNote: いえいえ #1047; the textbook どういたしまして is only #4414

why: Attaches to any noun to make 'it depends on / it's up to X'. ni yoru covers part of this but not 'up to you'.

english: hard to (awkward or uncomfortable): iizurai = hard to say

english: meaning; point (imi nai = pointless; imi wakannai = makes no sense)

ja: 持ってくる・持っていく

freqNote: 持ってくる #813; 持っていく #4478 + 持って行く #6864

english: die; (hyperbole) be dying (shinu hodo = to death; tsukarete shinisou = I'm dead tired; shinu ka to omotta = I thought I'd die)

english: spacious, wide, broad / cramped, narrow, small (place); kao ga hiroi = knows everyone; kokoro ga semai = petty

freqNote: はあ #521 pools sighs and the flat 'yes'

english: warm (weather, food, drinks, a person). Full form atatakai
freqNote: 温かい #2240; contracted あったかい #3006; 暖かい #6200
why: The pool has atsui, samui and tsumetai but no 'warm', which is the pleasant middle used for weather, food and people.

ja: ついていく・ついてくる
english: go along with, follow / come along (watashi mo tsuite iku = I'll come too; tsuite kite = follow me; tsuite ikenai = I can't keep up)
freqNote: ついてくる #1860; ついていく #2834 (kanji spellings rank lower)
why: You say this to join someone's plan or to lead someone. It is the counterpart of tsurete iku (take someone along), and 'can't keep up' extends it to lessons and conversations.

english: I'm hungry (nodo kawaita = I'm thirsty; onaka ippai = I'm full)
freqNote: おなかすく #2781 as a unit; おなか #1253; masculine-rough 腹減った #4970
why: A state phrase said several times a day, alongside nemui and itai, which are already in D. It is fixed, so it has to be learned whole.

english: stop (someone or something); park (kuruma o tomeru); turn off (water); tomete! = stop him / stop it. tomaru = stop by itself
freqNote: rank of the とめる reading of 止める as the tool reports it
why: Transitive partner of tomaru. yameru means to stop doing something; tomeru means to stop a thing or a person (a car, a machine, a friend about to do something rash).

english: none, no (X); without (satou nashi de = without sugar); off / not OK (kyou wa nashi = it's off today; sore wa nashi = that's a no)
why: Attaches to any noun to mean 'without', and works on its own as 'there isn't any' or 'cancelled'. E-nai-de only covers verbs.

english: going smoothly, on track (junchou? = going well?; junchou da yo)
why: The standard check-in and status reply for work, study, health, relationships and projects. It applies to any topic.

english: exaggerated, over the top (oogesa da yo = you're exaggerating; oogesa ni iu = blow it up)
why: A reaction you can attach to any story or claim, and also a modest way to deflect praise.

english: motivated, keen (yaruki nai = can't be bothered / no motivation; yaruki deta = I'm fired up)
freqNote: やる気 #1776 (the tokenizer splits off ある/ない)
why: Applies to work, study, exercise and chores. 'yaruki nai' is the everyday way to say you can't be bothered. Its shape matches jishin aru and kyoumi aru, which are already in D.

english: smart, clever (atama warui = dumb). kashikoi = clever, a bit more formal
freqNote: 頭いい #7901, 頭がいい #9568. The tokenizer usually splits it into 頭 #375 + いい, so this undercounts. Synonym 賢い is #3471
why: 'Smart' is a basic way to describe people and ideas, and D has no word for it.

english: teacher, doctor; used as 'you' when addressing teachers, doctors and authors (senpai / kouhai = senior / junior)
why: A title that stands in for a pronoun. A learner with a tutor or doctor addresses them this way constantly. It sits with -san, -chan and -kun.

english: question (shitsumon shite ii? = can I ask something?; ii shitsumon = good question)
why: A word for managing the conversation itself, alongside hanashi and imi in the pool. A learner needs it to ask permission to ask things.

english: word(s), language (sono kotoba wakaranai = I don't know that word; kotoba ga denai = I can't find the words)
why: A language word that pairs with imi. Learners need it to point at the word they didn't catch.

ja: 持って行く・持って来る
freqNote: rank of 持ってくる; 持っていく #4478
why: Japanese has no single verb for bring/take; it is motsu + -te kuru/iku. 'nani motte ikeba ii?', 'motte kuru ne', 'motte itte ii?'. Learners get stuck on 'bring' without this chunk.

english: lose (an item); get rid of (saifu nakushita = I lost my wallet)
freqNote: rank of kana なくす; 亡くす (lose a person) #2339 is separate
why: Losing things happens on every topic. otosu means drop, and nakunaru means 'it went missing' with no one responsible; nakusu is 'I lost it'.

english: keep (a promise, rule, time); protect (yakusoku mamotte ne = keep your promise)
why: The verb for keeping your word or keeping to rules and times. Drama inflates its 'protect' sense, but the keep-a-promise use is daily.

english: (this one) for sure, precisely (kondo koso = this time for sure; sore koso = exactly that)
why: Emphatic particle for 'THIS one, not the other': 'kondo koso katsu', 'ima koso', 'kochira koso'.

english: at most, at best (seizei ichi-jikan = an hour at most)
why: An upper-limit approximator that pairs with the pool's at-least items: 'seizei sanbyaku-en gurai', 'seizei futsuka'.

english: one or the other, either one (docchi ka ni shite = pick one; docchi ka to iu to = if anything, I'd say)
freqNote: tokenizer splits; rank of どっち (どっちか itself #33972)
why: Completes the docchi row. 'docchi ka to iu to' is also a handy hedge: 'if I had to say'.

polite: konna kanji desu / donna kanji desu ka
ja: こんな感じ・どんな感じ
english: like this, this sort of way / what's it like?, how's it going?
freqNote: tokenizer splits; rank of 感じ
why: 'donna kanji?' asks what a job, place or person is like. 'konna kanji de ii?' checks your work, and 'sonna kanji' means 'yeah, something like that'. This is separate from the -tte kanji ending.

english: motivation, drive (yaru ki nai = can't be bothered; yaru ki deta = I'm fired up)
why: Talks about motivation for any task: 'kyou yaru ki zero', 'yaru ki aru no?', 'yaru ki ga denai'. It works like kibun and choushi.

english: in a sense, in a way (aru imi sugoi = impressive, in a way)
why: Frames a strong claim as partial: 'aru imi tadashii', 'aru imi rakki'. aru teido hedges degree; aru imi hedges the framing.

english: maybe next time, another time (soft no to an invitation)
freqNote: tokenizer splits; rank of 今度 (また #91)
why: The standard face-saving close to a refusal ('gomen, kyou wa chotto... mata kondo ne'). It can also be a sincere 'let's do it another time'.

english: (someone else) shows signs of feeling / wants to (kowagatteru = is scared; ikitagatteru = is keen to go)
freqNote: tokenizer splits the suffix; rank of 嫌がる (怖がる #7163, 欲しがる #8352, bare たがる #52822)
why: Japanese doesn't state other people's feelings or wants directly: 'kodomo ga ikitagatteru', 'iyagatteru', 'hoshigatteta'. It is needed to talk about third persons.
